findings.title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` on `AssignmentSource` evaluates `timezone.now()` once when the module is imported, so every `AssignmentSource` instance created without an explicit `queued` argument will receive the module import timestamp rather than the time the instance was created. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` from `dataclasses` so that a fresh timestamp is generated per instance.

findings.title: Passing `assignment_source` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound` breaks concrete integrations
findings.body: `sync_assignee_outbound` now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. However, in `src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py`, `assignment_source` was added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature (line 416) instead of `sync_assignee_outbound` (line 397), and concrete `IssueSyncIntegration` implementations (such as Jira, Jira Server, GitHub, GitLab, VSTS, etc.) define `def sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` or without `**kwargs`. Any integration whose `sync_assignee_outbound` does not accept `**kwargs` or `assignment_source` will raise `TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'` whenever an issue is assigned in Sentry (when `assignment_source` is `None`) or synced from another integration.
